title: Microkernel fragmentation and soft-eviction scrap
content:
Summary:
This is an informal capture of the week’s late-afternoon working group and a handful of ad-hoc tests we ran on microkernel fragmentation and a new soft-eviction prototype. High-level: fragmentation under mixed-length chat traffic is causing uneven GPU memory utilization across microkernels, which in turn reduces effective batch coalescing and spikes tail latency during tail-heavy intervals. The soft-eviction prototype (v0.1) reduces OOM-triggered stalls but introduces extra KV cache churn that affects p99 generation latency in short-dialog workloads.

Attendees (quick):
- Asha Patel (notes)
- Miguel Ortega
- Liam Chen
- Rosa Kim
- Daniel Vega (oncall)
- two contractors (kernel-fiddle pairing)

Context / motivation:
- Goal: improve steady-state throughput without regressing p99 for short, single-turn calls (our tasking from product: keep hosted p99 <= 220ms for short prompts under mixed traffic).
- Current problem: microkernels get small fragmented allocations as KV cache entries are created/evicted per-session, preventing contiguous pooling and leading to more frequent slab switching.
- Observable effect: decreased coalescing opportunity for microbatcher (fewer compatible requests found within enqueue window), higher queue jitter.

What we measured (experiments run Aug 29–31):
- Baseline (canary pool) traffic replay: 10k requests, median length 48 tokens, 15% long dialogues (>1k tokens).
- Memory fragmentation metric (L1): increased by ~28% vs ideal contiguous baseline (measured by kernel allocator internal counters).
- Coalescing hit-rate: dropped from 73% -> 54% during long-dialog spike windows.
- p50/p90/p99 (short prompts): baseline 95/170/210ms -> with soft-eviction v0.1 100/185/245ms. p99 increased by ~35ms.
- OOM stalls: frequency dropped by ~60% with soft-eviction under synthetic spike.
- Extra KV churn: soft-eviction increased KV write amplification by ~22% (seen in telemetry counters).

Quick observations and hypotheses:
- Soft-eviction prevents catastrophic OOM stalls (win) but evicted items are frequently re-populated for hot sessions, causing looped write/delete thrash that harms the microbatcher.
- Fragmentation seems correlated with session churn pattern: many short sessions interleaved with a few long sessions fragment free lists.
- Current slab sizes were tuned for larger steady sessions; we need to revisit microkernel slab sizing and an adaptive slab compaction trigger.

Ideas we sketched (brain dump):
1) Gentle compaction pass: background compactor that coalesces adjacent free fragments when GPU load is < 35% and wallclock quiet period > 250ms (low priority, low impact on latency).
2) Soft-eviction hysteresis: only evict items younger than X ms OR items with low access frequency in last N tokens. Avoid evicting recently-active sessions.
3) Eviction write-batching: accumulate KV deletions for the same kernel and apply as a single op during safe windows to reduce immediate churn.
4) Session affinity hint: mark hot sessions as "sticky" so we avoid evicting their KV entries even under memory pressure; this reduces re-population.
5) Microbatcher backpressure tweak: widen enqueue window by 5ms during fragmentation spikes to increase probability of coalescing without hurting median latency much.

Decisions made in meeting (tentative):
- Ship a controlled soft-eviction v0.2 to night canaries with hysteresis (idea 2) and deletion batching (idea 3). Miguel owns the PR (JIRA-RWD-2387).
- Implement a low-risk background compaction prototype (idea 1) in a separate branch for lab runs; do not roll to canary until we have safety guards. Rosa to spike.
- Re-run coalescing microbench with larger sample windows to validate backpressure tweak; Liam to update microbatch settings and collect new traces.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Miguel Ortega: land soft-eviction v0.2 PR with hysteresis + deletion batching, include toggle flag and telemetry counters for eviction-age and eviction-frequency. ETA: 2026-09-04.
- Rosa Kim: prototype background compactor (lab-only) and dashboard for fragmentation index. ETA: 2026-09-10 for initial lab results.
- Liam Chen: run coalescing backpressure matrix (enqueue windows of +0ms, +5ms, +10ms) against 3 traffic mixes and produce p50/p99 table. ETA: 2026-09-03.
- Daniel Vega: update oncall runbook to include a temporary flag to disable soft-eviction on canaries if KV write amplification crosses threshold. ETA: 2026-09-02.
- Asha (me): assemble short write-up for product showing tradeoffs and recommended next steps for the hosted SLA discussion. ETA: 2026-09-07.

Notes from the ad-hoc debug session (observed log excerpts, paraphrased):
- "kernel-3 alloc: slab-switch count=17 in 1s; free-fragment-count=132; batch-coalesce-window saw 3 potential ops"
- "kv-del amplify=1.18 session=usr-3291 last-access=12ms"
- "soft-evict: evicted=18 kept=124 (age>900ms), reverts=6"
- These logs indicate soft-eviction is correctly targeting older entries but reverts show some sessions immediately repopulate entries.

Risks and unknowns:
- Compaction CPU/GPU overhead: need to ensure compaction does not hurt latency when it runs. Must have safe throttle.
- Correct hysteresis thresholds are workload dependent; tuning on one customer’s traffic might harm others. Plan to A/B across canaries.
- Edge cases: streaming generation with function calls creates long-lived but low-access KV entries — hysteresis must avoid kicking these out incorrectly.

Experimental plan for next week:
- Deploy soft-evict v0.2 behind a feature flag to 5% canary pool; collect p50/p99/tail stalls and KV write amplification for 72 hours.
- Run compaction prototype in lab on a 4-node replay to measure CPU/GPU overhead and fragmentation drop; tune compaction interval.
- Run synthetic mixed-length replay to measure microbatch coalescing at enqueue windows {0, +5, +10}.
- Add telemetry: per-kernel fragmentation index, eviction-age histogram, re-population ratio (evicted-and-recreated within T ms).

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- What hysteresis values minimize re-population while still preventing OOMs? (suggested starting point: age > 800ms AND access_count_last_1s < 2)
- Should sticky-session hint be explicit API-level (product-facing) or internal signal inferred from request-rate?
- Is deletion-batching safe for multi-tenant kernels that also share KV namespaces? Need security check.

Misc (notes-to-self / quick tickets):
- Add test harness for eviction re-population on github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/evict-tests (small unit/bench).
- Add fragmentation metric to per-model dashboard and create alert when fragmentation-index > 40% for > 5m.

Appendix: short checklist for canary roll (for oncall):
- Flagpoint exists and can be toggled per-pool.
- Telemetry: eviction.age, eviction.count, kv.write-amplification, fragmentation.index, p99.latency.short-prompts.
- Roll back plan: disable feature flag, revert PR if persistent regressions, escalate to oncall.

Next sync: Tue 2026-09-07, 10:00 PST (kernel squad + SRE).

---
Notes tone: rough, intended to be a working capture. Will convert to a cleaner RFC if we decide to formalize the compactor + hysteresis approach.
